validation.summary: 9 defect(s) detected. Structural score: 0.956. Coverage score: 0.833. Hallucination score: 1.000. Semantic score: 1.000. Overall score: 0.800.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers the main buy/sell/cancel/query/save flows, but it still misses several required CTS responsibilities and contains a few semantic control-flow defects in the exception handling branches.

defects.description: Decision N11 does not distinguish the required cancel exception outcomes because both branches terminate immediately, so the decision has no behavioral effect beyond ending the flow.
defects.evidence: R39 requires handling "the instruction concerned has been implemented" and R40 requires handling "no matched instruction to be cancelled". In the diagram, both the implemented and no-match branches from N11 go directly to N10.
defects.suggested_action: Route the branches to distinct handling or outcome actions if different semantics are intended; otherwise model the cancel exception as a single terminal outcome without a redundant decision.

defects.description: Decision N19 does not distinguish the required query outcomes because both branches terminate immediately, so the decision has no behavioral effect beyond ending the flow.
defects.evidence: R51 requires handling "no matched data" as a query exception. Both outgoing branches of N19 go directly to N10, so the decision never changes behavior.
defects.suggested_action: If the no-data case requires a distinct outcome, route it to dedicated handling; otherwise remove the redundant decision and keep only the termination path.

defects.description: The core CTS responsibility to complete stock trading is not explicitly represented as a distinct CTS action.
defects.evidence: R1 states that the central trading system is to complete the trading of stock. The diagram shows buy/sell actions and matching steps, but no explicit CTS activity representing completion of the trade itself.
defects.suggested_action: Add a CTS action that explicitly represents completing the stock trade, or clearly map an existing action to that responsibility if it is intended to cover R1.

defects.description: The prescribed matching rule is not explicitly represented as a guarded matching policy in the diagram.
defects.evidence: R3 requires the system to make a match under specifically prescribed rules. The diagram includes matching and a yes/no decision on stock match, but not the required prescribed matching policy itself.
defects.suggested_action: Add explicit policy/guard semantics for the matching rule, or annotate the matching step so it clearly reflects the prescribed matching conditions.

defects.description: The CTS interface-to-other-modules messaging responsibility is not modeled.
defects.evidence: R4 requires CTS to provide interfaces to send messages to other modules. The diagram has no action or lane representing outbound messaging interfaces.
defects.suggested_action: Add a CTS action for sending messages to external modules, or integrate that behavior into the relevant transaction completion flow.

defects.description: The post-processing step that produces new messages for network message promulgating is missing.
defects.evidence: R9 requires CTS to produce new messages and send them to network message promulgating after dealing with instructions from trade client serve. The diagram ends the transaction flows without any message production or outbound delivery step.
defects.suggested_action: Add the message-generation and handoff behavior to the diagram, linked after instruction processing.

defects.description: Authorization for system manager access to CTS information is not modeled.
defects.evidence: R10 requires that the system manager be authorized to access information in CTS. The diagram contains no management access path, authorization check, or related action.
defects.suggested_action: Add a management-access branch with an authorization condition for accessing CTS information.

defects.description: The maintainer crash-recovery behavior is absent from the diagram.
defects.evidence: R14 states that when the system crashes down, maintainers can find the cause and fix it. No crash-handling or recovery path is shown.
defects.suggested_action: If this behavior is in scope for the activity diagram, add a crash handling/recovery branch for maintainers.

defects.description: The maintainer support for modifying the program when new requirements arise is absent from the diagram.
defects.evidence: R15 requires maintainers to modify the program when new requirements should be supported. The diagram does not model any maintenance/update activity.
defects.suggested_action: Add a maintenance/update path if the diagram is intended to cover maintainer responsibilities.

strengths: The main transaction flows for buy, sell, cancel, save trade information, and query trade information are represented.
The diagram includes the required actor lanes for Transaction User Interface, Central Trading System, Security Account Management, and Trading System Management-related behavior.
The buy/sell flows follow the expected order of receive/save, match, trade, and modify steps.
